bug.title: Every rebalance date's window carries the snapshot's entire history, so per-date sandbox cost grows with the data window rather than with what a signal can use
bug.symptoms: orchestrator._evaluate._materialize_from_context (~line 372) reads every bars partition at or before the decision date for every PIT-universe symbol. On the 2019–2026 archive, a 2026 date serializes about 150k rows into the sandbox.
bug.reproduction_steps: Time materialize plus serialize_window for the archive config's last date against its first. The cost grows linearly with history.
bug.expected: - The evaluation config gains an optional key max_history_days: a positive int, default 400, documented in deploy/campaign/evaluation-config.example.json. - The materializer reads only partitions dated in (decision_date − max_history_days, decision_date]. The PIT universe rule is unchanged. - Truncation applies to every node, real and null alike. - The authoring declaration states the depth so agents write against it. The bars accessor's returns_notes, or stream_columns' sibling note, says "each window carries at most N trailing daily candles per symbol; a longer lookback returns what exists". N is read from the evaluation context when one is configured, and is absent otherwise. - test_window_history_cap.py covers, on a tmp sealed snapshot: - a window at a late date carries only the last N days - an early date carries everything available - the default applies when the key is absent - a non-positive value is refused at config load with a named error - the declaration names N It passes under pytest-xdist.
bug.actual: Root cause: the window is the whole history at or before t, because nothing bounds its depth.
bug.constraints: Window truncation at t, the PIT universe and the contract's accessors are unchanged No file outside the five listed is edited Do not edit docs/user-journeys/

bug.title: A campaign evaluates its nodes one at a time, so a 32-root campaign uses one of 16 cores
bug.symptoms: The 32-root campaigns of 2026-10-08 evaluated roots sequentially, with one gVisor sandbox alive at any moment and the host at about 6% CPU. Evaluation dominates wall time, since authoring all 32 roots takes about 10 min.
bug.reproduction_steps: Run the offline campaign e2e with 8 roots and time it. Wall time equals the sum of per-node times.
bug.expected: - The evaluation config gains an optional key evaluation_workers: an int from 1 to 16, default 4. - Root evaluation, and a round's child evaluations, run on a bounded thread pool of that size. Each node still runs in its own sandbox. Concurrent runsc containers use distinct container ids and the existing state root; verify that they never collide. - Results are identical to evaluation_workers=1: - the same node rows, scores and ledger rows (set-equal) - node_evaluated events emitted in the deterministic order a serial run would emit them, i.e. buffered and released in node order - the same stop_reason - one campaign's events are never interleaved with another's - SQLite writes (ledger, tree, stores) stay correct under concurrency. They are serialized through the existing store connections or a single writer lock, never two writers in one transaction, so no "database is locked" escapes. - A failing node never cancels its siblings. - test_concurrent_evaluation.py, with the stub executor the offline e2e already uses: - evaluation_workers 1 and 4 produce identical persisted rows and identical event order - 4 workers are at least 2.5× faster on 8 nodes with a sleeping stub executor - a raising node leaves its siblings evaluated - out-of-range values are refused at config load It passes under pytest-xdist.
bug.actual: Root cause: the round loop and root planting call evaluate_node serially.
bug.constraints: Determinism of every persisted record and of the event stream is unchanged No file outside the three listed is edited Do not edit docs/user-journeys/
